items.title: dtcc-dtc · New build
kv: DTC Tokenization Service: published launch scope (At-a-Glance sheet)

Canton Network (token standard CIP-56) - at launch · DTCC private network on Besu (token standard ERC-20) - at launch · Stellar (token standard SEP-41) - anticipated 2027 · Arc from Circle (token standard ERC-20) - anticipated 2027

DTCC's undated one-page sheet lists 25 securities available to tokenize at launch (select large-cap Russell 1000 names, 'expanding across the index', select ETFs, a select set of U.S. Treasuries), with a '~$30T' figure labelled 'backed by securities held at DTC'. Conversion orders via UI or API 2 a.m.-6 p.m. ET on business days, targeting 15 minutes or less; 24/7 peer-to-peer transfers between registered wallets; '1:1' intra-chain transfers between DTC-registered wallets; wallet registration via the UI for select third-party wallets; official books and records remain with DTC. Networks: Canton (CIP-56) and DTCC's private Besu network (ERC-20) under 'Live at Launch'; Stellar (SEP-41) and Arc (Circle) (ERC-20) anticipated in 2027. 'What's Next' lists single sign-on and maker-checker controls, expanded corporate-action servicing, a consolidated stock record across book-entry and on-chain positions, and on-chain netting and digital cash. Roadmap 'indicative and subject to change' and subject to the applicable SEC No-Action Letter.

Scope sheet, not a launch notice; undated; names no launch day; the 25 securities are not listed. The sheet does not say cross-chain movement is out of scope; it only describes transfers as 'intra-chain'. DTCC's live-production-trades page (checked 2026-10-19) still says 'expected October 2026 launch'.

Verdict: narrowed · Evidence quote: 25 ... securities available to tokenize at launch; Official books and records remain with DTC. · Reason: Source is DTCC's own and supports 'announced'. Narrowed: the sheet ties '1:1' to intra-chain wallet transfers, not to backing; '~$30T' is a bare label, not stated as 'eligible assets'; 'cross-chain outside initial scope' is not stated. Full name 'The Depository Trust Company' does not appear (only 'DTC').

items.title: dtcc-dtc · New build
kv: The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (no subsidiary named)

DTCC says its Collateral AppChain, 'a shared infrastructure platform for collateral', is expected to go live in Q4 2026 and will use Chainlink Runtime Environment for orchestration, data and automation of eligibility, valuation, margining, collateral optimization, settlement and related post-trade workflows. Chainlink's Sibos recap (Sep 29, updated Oct 1, 2026) says Chainlink and DTCC demonstrated on stage how Chainlink Fulcrum 'executed a cross-chain securities financing transaction'.
Planned capability with a target quarter; no live date, operating entity, chain or participant has been published. The Sibos demonstration is not production.

Verdict: narrowed · Evidence quote: is expected to go live in Q4 2026 · Reason: State 'roadmap' and Q4 2026 target confirmed by DTCC's own release. Narrowed: DTCC lists 'valuation', not 'pricing'; Chainlink's recap says 'will use' (not 'will leverage') and describes a 'securities financing transaction', not specifically a repo. The Sibos demo rests only on Chainlink's page; no DTCC document for it was cited.

items.title: dtcc-dtc · New deal
kv: Oasis Pro Markets LLC (Ondo Finance subsidiary)
Oasis Pro Markets LLC · The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (operator of Fund/SERV as named in the release)

Oasis Pro Markets LLC, an SEC-registered broker-dealer and noticed alternative trading system owned by Ondo Finance, joined DTCC's Fund/SERV fund-order network as a member and 'can now transact' with fund companies and distributors; DTCC calls it the first tokenization platform in Fund/SERV.

Membership is in effect, but no transaction is disclosed, and distribution of Ondo tokenized funds through traditional distributors is described as future ('paves the way'). Fund/SERV is a fund-processing service, not the DTC Tokenization Service.

Verdict: confirmed · Evidence quote: can now transact with fund companies, wealth platforms, and service providers · Reason: DTCC's own release, dated Sep 16, 2026, names Oasis Pro Markets LLC, 'first tokenization platform to participate' in Fund/SERV; no transaction disclosed; 'paves the way' for distribution is future. DTCC subsidiary operating Fund/SERV is not named. The 'live_available' state reflects membership in effect only.

items.title: dtcc-dtc · Legal event: Proposed rule change to modernize the Direct Registration System (DRS): DRS access through SPA on the DTCC Portal and by API/MQ messaging, retirement of certain legacy PTS/PBS functions and CCF batch processing for some DRS transactions, and required Centralized Billing of DRS Agent pass-through fees through DTC (six new fee-schedule entries). DTC's existing 5% collection charge is applied to these pass-through fees; the filing says it is not a new fee. Expected implementation Nov 13, 2026 (pending approval), and no later than January 2027 if that date is missed. No mention of tokenization or distributed ledgers.
kv: Filed Sep 29, 2026 (File No. SR-DTC-2026-012; Release No. 34-106552); notice published Oct 5, 2026; comments due Oct 26, 2026.

Verdict: narrowed · Evidence quote: The five-percent collection charge is not a new fee · Reason: Release number, file number, 91 FR 63327, Sep 29 filing, Oct 5 publication and Oct 26 comment deadline all confirmed. Narrowed: the 5% charge is an existing charge extended, not a new one; added the January 2027 fallback.
